common_name: Superbena Pink Shades Verbena (Powder Blue-Eyed Rose-Pink Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full to part sun; the star-shaped florets show a distinctive powder-blue eye ringed with hot pink that shifts the overall effect toward rose rather than the flatter pink of many bedding verbena.

directions: Superbena Pink Shades bears clusters of rose-pink, star-shaped florets with a small powder-blue eye and hot-pink center, giving the umbels more depth and contrast than a single flat shade of pink. Growth is vigorous and strongly trailing in the Superbena tradition, mounding 6-12 inches tall while spreading a somewhat tighter 12-14 inches, which makes it a good fit for smaller combination pots as well as full-size hanging baskets and landscape beds. Grow in full to part sun in well-drained soil, watering only as the top inch dries since the line is bred for drought and heat tolerance with reduced feeding needs compared with many bedding annuals. It blooms continuously from planting until frost without deadheading, draws butterflies, and has performed as a top selection in regional trial gardens alongside other Superbena colors already common in the trade.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbena Pink Shades Verbena Grower Information
Penn State Extension Flower Trials

common_name: Superbena Raspberry Verbena (Bright Magenta-Pink Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full to part sun; the saturated magenta-pink coloring reads brighter and cooler-toned than Superbena Burgundy or Wine under midday light.

directions: Superbena Raspberry carries bright magenta-pink flowers in the large, dense umbels typical of the series, contrasting sharply against dark green foliage and offering a cooler, brighter pink than the deeper wine and burgundy Superbena shades already in wide use. The habit is vigorous and strongly trailing, mounding 6-12 inches tall and spreading up to 24 inches, which suits hanging baskets, raised containers, and groundcover plantings equally well. Grow in full to part sun in well-drained soil, allowing it to dry out somewhat between waterings and feeding monthly with an all-purpose fertilizer rather than the heavier feeding many bedding annuals need. It blooms from early summer into fall without deadheading, attracts butterflies, resists deer browsing, and holds color well through extended summer heat.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbena Raspberry Verbena Grower Information
Louisiana State University AgCenter - Heat-Tolerant Verbena for Gulf South

common_name: Superbena Scarlet Star Verbena (Red Star-Shaped White-Eyed Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full to part sun; the narrow white eye at each flower's center gives the bright scarlet-red umbels a star-pattern effect similar in concept to Estrella Voodoo Star but in a true red rather than red-and-white bicolor.

directions: Superbena Scarlet Star produces bright red, star-shaped florets with a small white eye at the center, giving the umbels a crisp, patterned look rather than the flat solid red of Superbena Red. Plants are vigorous and strongly trailing, mounding 6-12 inches tall and spreading up to 24 inches, functioning well as a spiller in mixed containers and window boxes or as a flowering groundcover in beds. Grow in full to part sun in well-drained soil, letting the top inch dry between waterings since the selection was bred for strong disease resistance and holds up to humid summer conditions that cause mildew on older trailing verbena. It flowers continuously from early summer to fall frost without deadheading and draws butterflies throughout the season.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbena Scarlet Star Verbena Grower Information
Mississippi State University Extension - Verbena Trial Notes

common_name: EnduraScape Pink Bicolor Verbena (AAS-Winning Two-Tone Pink Landscape Verbena)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; this selection was a 2017 All-America Selections national winner and has also received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for landscape performance.

directions: EnduraScape Pink Bicolor bears soft pink flowers that intensify toward a deeper rose center, giving each cluster a two-tone glow that trial judges singled out as unusually vibrant among landscape verbena. It forms a dense, fast-spreading, low mat that blooms continuously from spring through fall frost with little dieback in summer heat, and the breeding line is noted for tolerating both extended drought and surprisingly cold winter temperatures for a verbena once established. Grow in full sun in well-drained, average soil, watering deeply but infrequently since overwatering is more likely to cause problems than underwatering. Its vigorous, weed-suppressing habit makes it well suited to mass plantings, slopes, and hot, sunny borders where the mildew that shortens the season on older verbena selections is rarely an issue.
sources: All-America Selections - Verbena EnduraScape Pink Bicolor National Winner
Ball Horticultural Company - EnduraScape Verbena Series
Royal Horticultural Society - Plant Finder

common_name: EnduraScape Red Verbena (Mildew-Resistant Heat-Tolerant Red Landscape Verbena)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Red is one of the true scarlet releases in the EnduraScape line and holds its color without fading through peak summer heat.

directions: EnduraScape Red forms the same dense, ground-hugging mat as the rest of the series, carrying bright scarlet-red flower clusters continuously from spring through fall frost without a significant mid-summer slowdown. It was bred specifically for resistance to powdery mildew, the fungal disease that commonly disfigures and shortens the bloom season of older verbena cultivars in humid climates, and it holds up to extended heat better than many bedding annuals in its color class. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil and water deeply but infrequently once established, since the series tolerates dry spells far better than consistently wet ground. A light shearing after the first big spring flush keeps the mat tight and encourages a fresh wave of bloom into fall.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company - EnduraScape Verbena Series
North Carolina State Extension - Annual Bedding Plant Trials

common_name: EnduraScape White Verbena (Pure White Mildew-Resistant Landscape Verbena)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; the clean white flowers hold their color all season rather than cycling to a dingy cream the way some older white verbena selections do by midsummer.

directions: EnduraScape White produces clean, pure white flowers over a dense, spreading, trailing mat that stays full and heavily branched from the nursery pot through the landscape. Like the rest of the series it was selected for strong resistance to powdery mildew and for tolerating both summer heat and drought once roots are established, making it a reliable low-maintenance choice where older white-flowered verbena often declines by midsummer. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, watering only as the top inch dries and avoiding overhead irrigation where possible to keep foliage dry and further reduce disease pressure. Its crisp white color pairs well as a contrast edge or filler among the brighter EnduraScape and Superbena colors already common in mixed beds and containers.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company - EnduraScape Verbena Series
University of Georgia Trial Gardens

common_name: EnduraScape White Blush Verbena (Soft Pink-Flushed White Landscape Verbena)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; the gentle pink flush toward each flower's center distinguishes this selection from the pure-white EnduraScape White at a glance.

directions: EnduraScape White Blush carries white flowers with a soft pink flush concentrated toward the center of each cluster, giving the mat a gentler, blended look than the crisp pure white of its sibling selection. It shares the series' dense, spreading, mildew-resistant habit and tolerates both summer heat and dry spells once established, blooming continuously from spring through fall frost with minimal dieback. Grow in full sun in well-drained, average soil, watering deeply but infrequently and skipping supplemental feeding beyond an occasional light application, since overly rich soil tends to push foliage at the expense of bloom. Its soft blended coloring works especially well as a transition color between bolder reds and purples in mixed landscape plantings.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company - EnduraScape Verbena Series
North Carolina State Extension - Annual Bedding Plant Trials

common_name: EnduraScape Hot Pink Verbena (Vivid Pink Mildew-Resistant Landscape Verbena)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; the saturated hot-pink color stays vivid through summer heat rather than bleaching out the way some older pink verbena selections do.

directions: EnduraScape Hot Pink covers its dense, spreading mat in vivid, saturated pink flowers from spring through fall frost, giving a punchier color statement than the softer EnduraScape Pink Bicolor and White Blush selections in the same series. It shares the line's strong resistance to powdery mildew and tolerates heat and drought well once established, making it a reliable choice for mass plantings and slopes where disease and water stress typically take a toll on older verbena cultivars. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, watering deeply but infrequently rather than keeping the root zone constantly moist. A light shearing after the initial spring flush keeps the planting tight and renews heavy bloom for the remainder of the season.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company - EnduraScape Verbena Series
University of Georgia Trial Gardens

common_name: EnduraScape Purple Verbena (Rich Purple Mildew-Resistant Landscape Verbena)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; the rich purple flowers give strong contrast against the warmer reds and pinks elsewhere in the EnduraScape line.

directions: EnduraScape Purple blankets its dense, fast-spreading mat in rich purple flower clusters continuously from spring through fall frost, rounding out the cooler end of the series' color range alongside EnduraScape Blue. Breeding emphasis on powdery mildew resistance and heat tolerance carries through to this color, so plants typically stay full and floriferous through humid summer conditions that cause older verbena cultivars to thin out and decline. Grow in full sun in well-drained, average soil, watering deeply but infrequently once roots are established and avoiding overly rich or constantly wet soil. Its vigorous, weed-suppressing spread makes it a practical, low-maintenance choice for slopes, medians, and large sunny beds.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company - EnduraScape Verbena Series
North Carolina State Extension - Annual Bedding Plant Trials

common_name: Santos Purple Verbena (Dense-Flowering Improved Rigid Verbena)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts after frost danger passes in well-drained, dry to moderately moist soil in full sun; 'Santos Purple' stays lower and denser-flowering than the wild species of sandpaper verbena already grown for mass plantings.

directions: 'Santos Purple' is a selected, denser-flowering form of sandpaper verbena that keeps the species' rough, sandpapery-textured foliage but stays shorter and more compact, forming low mounds packed with deep purple-magenta flower clusters from late spring through summer. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil and expect excellent drought tolerance once established, since the plant resents consistently wet ground far more than dry spells. It spreads steadily to a wide mat, making it a good choice for borders, slopes, and large containers where its bold color and long bloom season outweigh its somewhat coarse texture. It is a strong butterfly and pollinator plant and holds up to powdery mildew pressure better than many older rigid verbena selections.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society - Verbena rigida 'Santos' Plant Profile

common_name: Buenos Aires Verbena (Tall Well-Branched Purpletop Vervain)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before the last frost, keeping the mix evenly moist under strong light since germination is naturally slow and uneven; transplant into lean, well-drained soil in full sun once frost danger has passed.

directions: 'Buenos Aires' keeps the full, towering stature of wild purpletop vervain, reaching 4 to 5 feet or more on an upright, well-branched framework of square, wiry stems topped with clustered lilac-purple flower heads that trial observers note run slightly larger and more numerous than the species type. Grow in full sun in lean, well-drained soil, since overly rich or wet ground produces floppier growth that is more prone to toppling in wind and rain. It self-sows readily where winters are mild, so deadhead spent flower heads if volunteer seedlings are not wanted the following year. The airy, see-through habit makes it a favorite for the back of mixed borders or planted in drifts through shorter perennials, and its long nectar-rich bloom season draws butterflies, bees, and hummingbirds from summer into fall.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden - Plant Finder
Thompson & Morgan - Verbena 'Buenos Aires' Growing Guide
